words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: He is aware of the danger.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到危险。
words.en: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

words.ex: His behavioral changes worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为变化让他的父母担心。
words.en: Relating to the way in which someone behaves.

words.tr: adj. 无数的；多的；数不清的；
words.ex: There are countless stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数颗星星。
words.en: Too numerous to count.

words.ex: He does arithmetic every day with his little sister.
words.ex_cn: 他每天和妹妹一起做算术。
words.en: Arithmetic is the part of mathematics that deals with the addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of numbers.

words.ex: He consistently arrives at school on time.
words.ex_cn: 他一贯准时到校。
words.en: In a way that does not vary; in the same way over time.

words.tr: adj. 一致的；始终如一的；
words.ex: His answers are consistent with the data.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案与数据一致。
words.en: Someone who is consistent always behaves in the same way, has the same attitudes towards people or things, or achieves the same level of success in something.

words.ex: His performance in the game was excellent.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的表现非常出色。
words.en: The act of performing a play, concert, or some other form of entertainment.

words.ex: He ignored the warning sign.
words.ex_cn: 他忽视了警告标志。
words.en: If you ignore someone or something, you pay no attention to them.

words.tr: adv. 急剧地；引人注目地；
words.ex: The temperature dropped dramatically overnight.
words.ex_cn: 夜间温度急剧下降。
words.en: In a way that is sudden, noticeable, or significant, often in a way that is intended to produce a strong effect.

words.tr: adj. 急剧的；引人注目的；戏剧（性）的；
words.ex: There was a dramatic increase in temperature yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 昨天温度急剧上升。
words.en: If something is dramatic, it happens or changes suddenly and noticeably.

words.ex: The youngster rode his bike to school every day.
words.ex_cn: 这个年轻人每天骑自行车去上学。
words.en: A youngster is a young person, especially a child or teenager.

words.tr: adj. 感激的；欣赏的；表示赞赏的
words.ex: She was appreciative of his help.
words.ex_cn: 她对他的帮助心怀感激。
words.en: If you are appreciative of something, you are grateful for it.

words.ex: He made an investment in a small business.
words.ex_cn: 他投资了一家小企业。
words.en: An investment is an amount of money that you invest in something.

words.ex: He invests money in stocks.
words.ex_cn: 他投资股票。
words.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by putting it in a bank, or buying shares or property.

words.tr:
adj. 警觉的；警惕的；
n. 警报；
v. （使）警惕；（使）戒备；
words.ex: The alert guard noticed the strange movement.
words.ex_cn: 这位警觉的警卫注意到了奇怪的动静。
words.en: If you are alert, you are paying full attention to things around you and are able to deal with anything that might happen.

words.ex: He showed excellence in math competitions.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学竞赛中表现出色。
words.en: The quality of being outstanding or extremely good.

words.tr: phrase. 理解；辨认出；书写；进展；设法应付；亲热
words.ex: I can't make out the words in this small print.
words.ex_cn: 我看不清这些小字。
words.en: to manage to see, hear, or understand someone or something with difficulty

words.ex: I am only too happy to help you with your project.
words.ex_cn: 我非常乐意帮助你完成你的项目。
words.en: Used to emphasize that you are very willing to do something or that you are very aware of something.

words.tr: phrase. 算不上是…的；不太好的；不怎样的
words.ex: He's not much of a cook.
words.ex_cn: phrase. 他算不上是个好厨师。
words.en: Used to indicate that someone or something is not very good at a particular activity or does not have a particular quality to a great extent.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 捞出；掏出；费力地取出（尤指从某处艰难地拿出某物）
words.ex: He fished out his keys from his pocket.
words.ex_cn: 他从口袋里把钥匙掏了出来。
words.en: To remove something from a place, especially with some difficulty.

words.tr: phrase. 对…不予理睬；轻易摆脱；漠然置之
words.ex: She managed to shrug off her troubles and continue with her work.
words.ex_cn: 她设法摆脱了烦恼，继续工作。
words.en: If you shrug something off, you ignore it or treat it as if it is not really important or serious.

words.tr: phrase. 表扬；鼓励；赞扬；拍拍背以示赞赏
words.ex: He gave me a pat on the back for a job well done.
words.ex_cn: 他因为我的出色工作而拍了拍我的背以示鼓励。
words.en: An expression of praise or congratulation.

words.ex: He will pass on the message to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会把消息转告给他的朋友。
words.en: To give something to someone else, especially after receiving it or using it; to continue moving forward; to die.

words.tr: phrase. 继续生存； 以...为主食, 靠...生活
words.ex: The old man lives on small donations from neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人靠邻居们的小额捐款继续生存。
words.en: To continue to exist or be remembered; to have a particular type of food or income as one's main source of sustenance.

words.ex: The glow of the fire warmed the room.
words.ex_cn: 火的炽热温暖了房间。
words.en: If something glows, it produces a dull, steady light.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.ex: His mood changed after he heard the good news.
words.ex_cn: 他听到这个好消息后，心情变了。
words.en: A mood is a temporary state of mind or feeling.

words.ex: The employee arrived at work early.
words.ex_cn: 这位雇员早早到达了工作地点。
words.en: An employee is a person who is paid to work for an organization or for another person.

words.ex: He loves reading poetry before bed.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在睡前读诗歌。
words.en: Poetry is the expression of ideas and feelings through the use of distinctive style and rhythm.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.ex: He crushed the can with his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手把罐子压碎了。
words.en: To crush something means to press it very hard so that its shape is destroyed or so that it breaks into pieces. It can also mean to defeat someone completely, or to make someone feel extremely upset or disappointed.

words.ex: He opposes the new law.
words.ex_cn: 他反对这项新法律。
words.en: If you oppose someone or something, you disagree with them and try to prevent them from doing something, or you try to change what they are doing.
